references.text: The boundary goes up to Beth-hogla and continues north of Beth-arabah. This text describes a similar boundary description that mentions the Arabah area.
Beth-arabah is mentioned as one of the cities in the wilderness, referring to the same geographical area by the Arabah valley.
This verse is part of the same boundary description of the tribe of Benjamin and describes the northern border going toward the wilderness.
The Arabah is mentioned as part of the wilderness area where Moses spoke to Israel, referring to the same geographical landscape.
The Sea of the Arabah (the Dead Sea) and the Arabah valley are mentioned in connection with the Israelites' crossing of the Jordan, the same area described in Joshua.
